plants.name: Cyclamen hederifolium
plants.description: Swept-back pink petals rise on slender stems from the woodland floor. Each flower has a darker blush at its throat. Marbled, heart-shaped leaves follow and make a silvery carpet through autumn and winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to mid-autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Woodlands and shaded gardens of southern Europe and the temperate Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: After pollination, the flower stalk coils like a spring and pulls the seed capsule down to the soil. Ants then carry the sticky seeds away.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: Fluffy, fragrant golden pom-poms cover the branches and glow against grey-green foliage. The tree is a bright sight at the end of the Australian winter and attracts many birds and insects.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (typically August to September)
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia and New South Wales
plants.funFact: Golden Wattle is Australia's national floral emblem, and the country celebrates Wattle Day every 1 September.

plants.name: Dimorphotheca sinuata
plants.description: Orange daisies with dark centers open toward the sun and turn whole hillsides into glowing carpets. When clouds roll in, the flowers fold shut.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (peaking late August to September)
plants.location: Namaqualand, in the Northern Cape of South Africa
plants.funFact: The flowers track the sun and close in cloudy weather or at night. Visitors are often advised to go on sunny afternoons for the best show.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Goblet-shaped lilac-pink blooms appear in meadows and gardens with no leaves around them. The bare stems look like crocuses that have come up in the wrong season.
plants.funFact: Despite the common name, it is not a true crocus, and it is highly toxic. Its leaves emerge in spring and die back long before the flowers appear.
